oncall-bot: :rotating_light: PAGED @sanjay - multiple streaming decode workers reporting CUDA OOMs, auto-escalation to on-call. stack: https://internal/pager/3034567890

sanjay: I’m on it. quick summary? impact?

elaine: Observed a sudden surge in streaming sessions at ~14:02 UTC, several decode-worker pods hit GPU OOM while handling long-running chat streams. Repro: a user sent a prompt with no max_tokens header and our default route allowed unbounded continuation. Node examples: decode-worker-12, decode-worker-19.

elaine: Logs (snip):
```
[2026-03-14T14:02:17Z] ERROR decode-worker-12: exception in generation loop: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY (cuCtxPushCurrent failed)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/srv/runtime/decode/stream_handler.py", line 412, in _stream_loop
    token = model.decode_step(...)
  File "/srv/runtime/model/runtime.cpp", line 1280, in run_decode
    check_cuda(cudaMalloc(&buf, size));
RuntimeError: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
```

kevin: 2 quick notes: 1) We recently deployed a tweak to default header parsing that inadvertently ignores all-caps headers for legacy SDKs — so many requests lost the "x-max-tokens" cap. 2) autoscaler couldn't react fast enough because batched KV cache growth kept tokens in-flight longer.

sanjay: That suggests unbounded generation + sustained batching caused memory pressure. Priority 1: stop further OOMs. Options: A) impose a hard token ceiling at the proxy layer B) throttle streaming routes to smaller concurrency C) evict large KV entries aggressively. I'll coordinate.

ops-bot: Runbook triggered: Incident playbook #decode-oom-stream started by @sanjay. Paging infra and SRE. Link: https://internal/runbook/decode-oom-stream

kevin: I can push a proxy-side patch to enforce per-request token ceilings. Patch ready in branch 'hotfix/proxy-enforce-ceil'. Plan: patch + rolling restart of proxy pods in region eu-west-1.

elaine: Confirmed customer-visible failures: we saw ~2200 dropped streaming sessions in eu-west-1 in the last 8 minutes, 7 requests returned 500/stream-closed, most retries succeeded but a few premium customers reported timeouts. Capturing sample request ids: r_8f1a, r_8f2b, r_8f5c.

support-liaison: Noted. Opening tickets and drafting outbound: initial impact note to affected accounts w/ CTA to escalate.

kevin: Applying hotfix now. Commands:
```bash
kubectl -n inference set image deploy/proxy proxy=image.build/redwood/proxy:hotfix-20260314
kubectl rollout status deploy/proxy -n inference --timeout=120s
```

kevin: Patch rolled out to proxy pods in eu-west-1. Rolling restart complete. Enforced header normalization and default hard cap 1024 tokens for streaming endpoints.

elaine: After patch, decode-worker OOM occurrences dropped significantly, but decode-worker-12 is still flapping and throwing CUDA mem errors on new sessions. Likely residual fragmentation.

sanjay: Short-term: cordon decode-worker-12 and drain in-flight sessions. Ops, please evict the node and spin up replacement.

ops-bot: kube-drain initiated: decode-worker-12 -> cordoned, draining pods. New node spawn requested from autoscaler.

elaine: After drain, memory defrag freed and new workers stable. Metrics: GPU mem usage 85% -> 60% after enforcement and drain. Token generation rate normalized.

kevin: Follow-up: we reverted the header parsing change and added a unit + integration test to prevent ignoring various header casings. Also added a middleware check that rejects requests without an explicit max_tokens when route config requires it (500 if missing).

support-liaison: Customer impact summary for SOC ticket: 10 accounts experienced degraded streaming between 14:02-14:12 UTC; 3 customers filed 500/timeout errors; all affected sessions retried by clients except two that required manual resends. Tickets created: INC-3241, INC-3242, INC-3243. Drafted outbound note for customers.

sanjay: Postmortem action items: 1) revert header parsing regression (done), 2) add proxy-enforced token ceiling (done), 3) make KV cache eviction adaptive to sequence length, 4) add streaming perf alert on rising mean token per-session, 5) run a chaos test for header-casing. Assign owners in the postmortem doc.
